_comment: PERFORMANCE BUDGETS — port Phase 0 / Gate A deliverable:
'establish bundle, answerability, memory, GPU, and audio-node budgets'.
THREE KINDS OF ENTRY, kept strictly separate so this file cannot overstate itself:
measured  — observed on v1.8.9 in this environment, with the command that produced it
budget    — a TARGET for the port, with the reasoning that sets it
unmeasured— explicitly NOT known, and WHY. A budget invented for something that
cannot be measured yet is a number nobody will honour.
⚠ EVERY LATENCY NUMBER IS PAIRED, 1x AND 4x CPU. The roadmap's own rule: Nick's
primary device is an iPhone, so a desktop number is the best case, not the case.
The two differ by 12x here, and the whole cold-boot arc (v1.8.5) existed because

environment._comment: Latency figures are environment-bound. Re-measure on a version bump; treat movement as a re-baseline decision, not a regression (Addendum D).

measured._comment: One file, one inline script. Transfer is NOT the problem — the network finishes in ~46ms. Compiling the script is.

_rationale: The current build ships 100% of the game before the first screen can answer.
ROADMAP 6a: the residual ~1.9s of cold boot is dominated by V8 compiling the
1.9MB inline script at 4x — 'the PAYLOAD problem the v2.0 port plan already owns'.
So the port's bundle budget is not really about bytes, it is about how much
CODE MUST COMPILE BEFORE THE FIRST INTERACTION. Code-splitting is the fix; the
250 KB figure is a starting target for the initial route, to be re-forecast

answerability._comment: PAINTED IS NOT ANSWERABLE — PROCESS_LAWS law 3. A gate can be drawn, hit-testable, and unable to reply because the main thread is blocked. bootperf measures both.

measured.profile: fresh (cold HTTP + cold V8 code cache), no save — the genuine first-run path
measured._comment: 12x spread between 1x and 4x. Painted is fine at both (111 / 355). ANSWERABLE is where it falls apart: 160 -> 1944. v1.8.5 already cut this from ~6440ms via _hdLater(); what remains is compile time.

_rationale: answerable_4x ≤ 1000ms is a ~2x improvement on today's 1944ms and is the single
most player-visible number in the port — it is the window a new player judges
the game in. It should FALL, not hold: module splitting is the entire point.
worstLongtask ≤ 200ms keeps any single task under the threshold at which input
feels dropped; today's worst is 754ms at 4x.

measured._comment: ⚠ THERE IS NO CONCURRENCY CAP. Greps for maxVoices / MAX_VOICE / activeVoices / concurrent find nothing. Audio is fully procedural (zero shipped .mp3/.ogg/.wav), so every utterance allocates its 10 nodes fresh. Nothing bounds how many can be in flight at once.

_rationale: §15 calls for mobile concurrency and streaming budgets and there is currently no
cap of any kind. 8 concurrent voices at 10 nodes each is 80, leaving headroom for
ambience and UI within a 120-node ceiling. These are STARTING targets — the
human listening test and a real phone profile should refine them.
Capping voices is also an audio-quality decision, not only a performance one:
a voice dropped because of a cap must be dropped gracefully.

_why: A meaningful memory budget needs the thing being measured to exist. Today's build
is immediate-mode Canvas 2D with an art cache capped at 1,200 entries and DPR
3 desktop / 2 touch (CLAUDE.md rule 9). The port's memory profile is dominated by
PixiJS textures, render targets and Spine-or-equivalent rigs — none of which exist
yet. Setting a JS-heap number now would be measuring the wrong program.
SET THIS AT THE PHASE 3 ENGINE PROOF, when there is a Pixi scene to profile.

carryForward._comment: Nick's 'phone runs hot' mandate — audited invariants that the port must not quietly relax.

_why: The current build uses NO WebGL — it is 2D canvas throughout, so there is no GPU
baseline to measure and nothing to compare a port number against. WebGL/WebGL2 is
the port's production baseline (§2.4), with WebGPU optional and never required.
SET THIS AT THE PHASE 3 ENGINE PROOF: draw calls, texture memory, and render-target
count per scene, measured on a phone.

howToReMeasure._comment: Always run BOTH arms. A single unthrottled number is what let the round-7 cold-boot outlier hide.
